images.title: 3 caps times 4 dresses
images.purpose: Shows a tree of choices: each of Estu's 3 caps goes with each of 4 dresses, making 12 outfits.
images.composition: Plain white background, lots of empty space around the main object, no scenery, no people, no extra text. A simple tree read from left to right: three cap nodes, each branching into four dress nodes.
images.exact_structure: On the left, exactly 3 amber (#E69F00) flat cap icons stacked vertically with even spacing. From each cap, exactly 4 thin grey lines fan out to the right, each ending at a small flat teal (#0072B2) dress icon; 12 dress icons in all, in one vertical column of 3 groups of 4. The label '3 caps' under the cap column, the label '4 dresses each' under the dress column, and the label '4 × 3 = 12' at the far right in a reddish purple (#CC79A7) rounded box. Exactly 3 caps, 12 branches, 12 dresses.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
images.takeaway: When every choice goes with every other choice, multiply the numbers of choices.
images.description: Shows a tree of choices: each of Estu's 3 caps goes with each of 4 dresses, making 12 outfits.
images.teaching_notes: Ask what changes if a fourth cap is added: 4 more branches, 16 outfits.

image_decisions.why: The tree of choices shows why combinations multiply instead of add.
